summary: The lecture covers terrestrial ecosystems focusing on deserts (hot and cold), grasslands (tropical and temperate), forest types by altitude/latitude, and ecological pyramids. It details adaptations, distribution, climate characteristics, and Indian context including ISFR forest cover data, density classifications, and specific species like Red Sanders. Key concepts include forest cover definitions, energy flow (10% rule), and pyramid inversions in aquatic/tree ecosystems.
points: Deserts cover 1/7th of Earth's surface; two types: hot deserts (Sahara, Thar) and cold deserts (Gobi, Patagonian, Ladakh).
Desert plants adapt via reduced leaves, thick cuticle, sunken stomata, CAM photosynthesis, extensive roots to conserve water.
Most deserts lie on western continental margins (trade wind belts); exceptions: Patagonian (rain shadow), Central Asian (continentality).
Grasslands occupy ~40% land surface; lie between desert and mountain climates with alternate wet/dry seasons.
Tropical grasslands (Savanna, Pampas, Veldt, Downs) have tall grasses, large herbivores; Temperate grasslands (Prairies, Steppes, Pampas, Downs) have short grasses, cold winters, 50-130 cm rainfall.
Forest types by altitude: Tropical evergreen (>200 cm rain), Tropical deciduous (100-200 cm), Subtropical, Temperate coniferous, Alpine (>3000m), Tundra.
ISFR 2021: India's forest cover 21.71%, tree cover 2.91%, total 24.62%; Forest cover defined as >10% canopy density over >1 hectare.
Largest forest cover area: Madhya Pradesh; Highest percentage: Mizoram; Highest increase: Andhra Pradesh; Highest loss: Arunachal Pradesh.
Density classes: Very Dense Forest >70%, Moderately Dense 40-70%, Open Forest 10-40%, Scrub <10% canopy density.
Ecological pyramids: Energy pyramid always upright (10% transfer rule); Biomass pyramid inverted in aquatic systems; Numbers pyramid inverted in tree ecosystems (insects > trees).
Red Sanders (Pterocarpus santalinus) endemic to Andhra Pradesh, native to India; listed under CITES.
Lichens and mosses are pioneer species surviving on bare rock without soil; Moringa (drumstick) is leguminous evergreen, minor forest produce, seeds used for biofuel.

check.q: Which of the following statements about desert distribution is correct?
opts: Most deserts are located on eastern continental margins due to trade winds
Cold deserts like Gobi and Patagonian are found in mid-latitudes due to continentality and rain shadow respectively
Hot deserts receive high rainfall during night due to maritime influence
Thar Desert is a cold desert located in the rain shadow of Western Ghats
